text.p: Brazilian star Emerson has reportedly walked out on Middlesbrough and insisted he will not be coming back.
But on Wednesday the English premier league club said the player had simply been given home leave and that they expected him back next week.
The four million pounds ($6.6 million) midfielder was said to have flown home to Brazil, blaming his wife Andrea's homesickness.
Speaking to the Sun from Brazil, Emerson is reported as saying: "My wife has found it impossible to come to terms with life in Middlesbrough.
"Manager Bryan Robson knows of the problems, but both he and the club believe Andrea and I will overcome them and report back for training next Tuesday.

"But I have told 'Boro quite clearly that I want to be released and sold as quickly as possible. They do not believe I am quite as serious as I am. If they insist I have to return, I will simply refuse to play. For anyone."
But Middlesbrough chief executive Keith Lamb told BBC radio on Wednesday: "I think there's no truth at all (in the reports).
"We've arranged for Emerson and his wife to return to Rio for a few days because of the cancellation of the games whilst the internationals are on next weekend.
"We made the arrangements for him and we fully expect him to come back on Tuesday or Wednesday."
After a good start to the season, Middlesbrough have slipped badly and are now sixth from the bottom.
